# wso2is_user (Resource)

Manages a user through the SCIM 2.0 API.

The provider only manages the attributes in your configuration. It leaves alone the attributes that the user sets in My Account, or that other systems set.

The server never sends passwords back. As a result, the provider cannot notice a password that someone changed outside Terraform. Use `password_wo` (Terraform 1.11 or later) to keep the password out of the state, or `ask_password` to let the user choose a password. To import a user, use the user's ID.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "wso2is_user" "alice" {
  username    = "alice"
  given_name  = "Alice"
  family_name = "Smith"
  email       = "alice@example.com"
  emails = {
    work = "alice@corp.example"
  }
  phone_numbers = {
    mobile = "+15551234567"
  }
  attributes = {
    "urn:scim:wso2:schema:country"                                          = "Sri Lanka"
    "urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department" = "Engineering"
  }
  password_wo         = var.alice_password # Terraform 1.11+
  password_wo_version = 1
}

# Invite a user to set their own password (needs an email provider).
resource "wso2is_user" "bob" {
  username     = "bob"
  email        = "bob@example.com"
  ask_password = true
}

variable "alice_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `username` (String) Username, without the user store prefix. Changing it replaces the user (WSO2 does not support renaming).

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `ask_password` (Boolean) Create the user without a password and email them a link to set one (needs an email address and the Ask Password governance setting). The provider only uses this value when it creates the user.
- `attributes` (Map of String) Other SCIM attributes, by path. Core attributes use their name, such as `title`, `locale` or `name.middleName`. Extension attributes start with their schema URN, for example `urn:scim:wso2:schema:country`, `urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:enterprise:2.0:User:department` or `urn:scim:schemas:extension:custom:User:<custom claim>`. All values are strings. The provider converts booleans and numbers with the server's SCIM schema. Separate the values of a multi-valued attribute with commas.
- `disabled` (Boolean) Whether the account is disabled. This sets `urn:scim:wso2:schema:accountDisabled`, which needs the account disabling governance connector (`account.disable.handler`).
- `display_name` (String) Display name.
- `email` (String) Primary email address (`http://wso2.org/claims/emailaddress`), used for notifications and account recovery.
- `emails` (Map of String) More email addresses, by type (`work`, `home` or `other`). For several verified addresses, use the `urn:scim:wso2:schema:emailAddresses` attribute instead.
- `family_name` (String) Last name (`name.familyName`).
- `given_name` (String) First name (`name.givenName`).
- `locked` (Boolean) Whether the account is locked (`urn:scim:wso2:schema:accountLocked`). The server also locks the account after failed logins when account locking is on.
- `nick_name` (String) Nickname.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) The user's password. It must meet the tenant's password policy. Terraform stores it in the state. Use `password_wo` instead to keep it out of the state.
- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) A write-only password (Terraform 1.11 or later). The provider sends it to the server but never stores it in the state. To set a new password, change it and increase `password_wo_version`.
- `password_wo_version` (Number) Increase this number to send a new `password_wo`.
- `phone_numbers` (Map of String) Phone numbers by type: `mobile`, `home`, `work`, `other`.
- `user_store` (String) User store domain. The default is `PRIMARY`. Changing it replaces the user.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) User ID (SCIM `id`).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_user.alice <user_id>
```
